# Load package

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

```

# Introduction

This vignette demonstrates the use of selected Tidyverse packages to explore MTA Subway Hourly Ridership data for December 2024.

```{r}
package_table <- tibble(
  Package = c("dplyr", "ggplot2", "readr", "stringr", "forcats", "lubridate"),
  `Functions used` = c(
    "mutate(), select(), group_by(), summarize()",
    "ggplot(), geom_col(), geom_line(), geom_point(), geom_text(), labs()",
    "read_csv()",
    "str_remove()",
    "fct_reorder()",
    "mdy_hm(), hour()"
  ),
  Purpose = c(
    "Data cleaning and manipulation",
    "Data visualization",
    "Importing CSV data",
    "Removing text from fare categories",
    "Ordering fare categories",
    "Working with timestamps"
  )
)

knitr::kable(package_table, caption = "Tidyverse Packages and Functions Used")
```

# Import data

```{r}
url<-"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lhamo07/Data-607-fall/refs/heads/main/MTA_Subway_Hourly_Ridership__Dec-2024.csv"
mta_raw<-read_csv(url)

```

```{r}
# Data Cleaning
mta_clean <- mta_raw %>%
  # remove text "OMNY - " from every fare_class_category since we are analyzing only Payment type 'OMNY'
  
  mutate(fare_class_category = str_remove(fare_class_category,
                                          "OMNY - ")) %>%
  # split transit timestamp
  mutate(
    datetime_obj = mdy_hm(transit_timestamp),
    transit_date = as.Date(datetime_obj),
    transit_time = format(datetime_obj, "%I:%M %p"),
    transit_hour = hour(datetime_obj)
  )
# select only necessary columns

mta_selected <- mta_clean %>%
  select(transit_date, transit_time, transit_hour,
         borough, fare_class_category, ridership)


```

```{r}

glimpse(mta_selected)

```

**which borough have the highest ridership?**

```{r}
riderShip_count_borough<-mta_selected%>%
  group_by(borough)%>%
  summarize(total_ridership=sum(ridership,na.rm = TRUE))

```

```{r}
ggplot(riderShip_count_borough,
       aes(x = borough, y = total_ridership, fill=borough)) +
  geom_col() +
# Display Y-axis values in regular number format with commas instead of scientific notation
scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +

  labs(
    title = "Total Subway Ridership by Borough (December 2024)",
    x = "Borough",
    y = "Total Ridership",
    fill = "Borough"

  ) +
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Among the four boroughs, Manhattan had the highest subway ridership, with 40,706,825 rides in December 2024. Brooklyn followed with 14,194,080 rides, while Queens recorded 8,638,361 rides. The Bronx had the lowest ridership, with 3,610,069 rides.

**Which fare categories are most commonly used?**

```{r}
mta_selected %>%
  group_by(fare_class_category) %>%
  summarize(total_ridership = sum(ridership, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    # Reorder fare categories from highest to lowest total ridership
  mutate(fare_class_category =
           fct_reorder(fare_class_category, total_ridership, .desc = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = fare_class_category, y = total_ridership)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(total_ridership)), 
            vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Total Ridership by Fare Category (December 2024)",
    x = "Fare Category",
    y = "Total Ridership"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

Full Fare was the most commonly used fare category, indicating that most recorded subway rides in this dataset were paid at the regular fare rate.

**What time of day has the highest subway ridership?**

```{r}
rider_time <- mta_selected %>%
  group_by(transit_date, transit_hour) %>%
  summarize(
    daily_ridership = sum(ridership, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(transit_hour) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_ridership = mean(daily_ridership),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

```

```{r}
ggplot(rider_time, aes(x = transit_hour, y = avg_ridership)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Daily Subway Ridership by Hour of Day (December 2024)",
    x = "Hour of Day",
    y = "Average Daily Ridership"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

The chart shows two major ridership peaks, around 8 AM and 5 PM. This suggests that subway ridership is highest during the morning and evening commuting hours.

# Conclusion

This analysis explored subway ridership by borough, fare category, and hour of the day in December 2024. Manhattan had the highest ridership, Full Fare was the most commonly used category, and peak ridership occurred around 8 AM and 5 PM.Tidyverse packages made it possible to clean, organize, summarize, and visualize the ridership data effectively.

# Limitations

Due to the large size of the original dataset, this analysis focuses only on December 2024. Therefore, the findings may not represent subway ridership patterns throughout the year.

**Data source:** <https://data.ny.gov/Transportation/MTA-Subway-Hourly-Ridership-2020-2024/wujg-7c2s/about_data>
